title: The Night Shift
logline: On steep, misted hill roads, an ambulance crew races between a district hospital and villages that are sometimes twenty minutes away and sometimes two hours, and every call is a small argument with time.

object.note: Object 8 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From what a death leaves behind to how fragile a life is before it ends: an ambulance crew on misted hill roads, arguing with time on every call.

thread_out.thread: When speed has done what it can, someone still comes: a village monk walking to house after house where someone is close to death.

requirements: A rural or hill-district ambulance service willing to permit filming under strict patient-privacy conditions
A crew willing to be followed for at least one full shift

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts describe four ways a life can end, and they say an early death often gets its chance through ordinary dangers such as carelessness, bad food, infection or illness left untreated. So care and skill still matter.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ජීවිතයක් නිම වන ආකාර හතරක් ඇති බවත්, අකල් මරණයට බොහෝ විට ඉඩ සැලසෙන්නේ නොසැලකිල්ල, නුසුදුසු ආහාර, බෝවන රෝග හෝ ප්‍රතිකාර නොකළ අසනීප වැනි සාමාන්‍ය අනතුරු නිසා බැවින් රැකවරණයට හා දක්ෂතාවයට තවමත් වටිනාකමක් ඇති බවත් ග්‍රන්ථ කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma names four kinds of death: when the lifespan runs out, when the force of the action that began the life runs out, when both run out together, and a cutting-off while both remain, which is untimely death. The Pradeepika says untimely death gets its opening through violence, poison, careless behaviour, unsuitable food, contagious illness and illness left untreated, and that a death that seemed to be coming could still be averted when those helping are skilled. It pictures the four as the ways an oil lamp goes out: the oil runs dry, the wick burns down, both at once, or a strong wind blows it out while oil and wick remain.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Headlights on wet hill roads, a call on the radio, first aid at a roadside or in a front room: every call becomes a race to keep a lamp out of the wind. Between calls, the crew's own words about the job show skill and fragility meeting, and the film never suggests why any particular person was hurt.

key_terms.en: death by cutting off; untimely death

lesson.caution: It does not mean 'it was their time' or 'it was their karma': the texts separate timely from untimely death, and no one can read a particular death as deserved.
lesson.builds_on: From what a death leaves behind, this film turns to how a death comes, and adds that life is fragile but not fated: care can sometimes keep the lamp out of the wind.
